features.t: VPC firewall rules (create, list, get, delete)
x: Hit count, last hit and Firewall Insights are not computed (empty rather than simulated numbers).

Every new network gets its default route (0.0.0.0/0 → default-internet-gateway). Static routes (priority, instance tags, next hop gateway/instance/IP) are evaluated; dynamic routes from Cloud Router BGP / VPN are not modeled. Internet egress needs an external IP or Cloud NAT.

features.t: Static IP addresses, regional and global (reserve, list, release)

x: networks.addPeering / removePeering are real: a peering is ACTIVE only once both networks peer, subnet routes are exchanged (non-transitive) and Connectivity Tests route across it. Custom-route import/export flags are stored but not applied; offline packet enforcement across peered networks is compiled but not covered by the real-packet test.

Real resource lifecycle: reserving an internal range (globalAddresses, purpose VPC_PEERING) is rejected if it overlaps an existing subnet or reservation on the network, and a servicenetworking.googleapis.com Connection can only reference ranges that are actually reserved. There is no real Google-managed service producer VPC behind the connection, so traffic to a private service endpoint (e.g. a Cloud SQL private IP) does not route across it in Connectivity Tests.

features.t: Network firewall policies (hierarchical / regional policy resources)
x: Regional network firewall policies only (no organization/folder hierarchy — Vyomi is single-project). Rules are evaluated for real: an associated policy's rules are checked BEFORE the network's classic VPC firewall rules (the real tier precedence), first match by priority wins, and Connectivity Tests trace through them. `goto_next` rules are stored and returned faithfully but evaluated as an implicit allow rather than deferring to the next tier.

features.t: VPC Flow Logs (Subnets / VLAN attachments / Cloud VPN tunnels)
x: Offline only, and only with netsim enforcement on (VYOMI_NETSIM_ENFORCE=1|auto, Docker compute backend): core/netsim/wiring.py reads the enforcer's real per-flow nft counters, renders GCP VPC Flow Log records (core/gcp_compute_core.py:gcp_flow_log_records, gated on each subnet's own flowLogs flag) and writes them as real Cloud Logging entries (logName compute.googleapis.com%2Fvpc_flows) from ONE persistent collector, so each apply reports only the counter DELTA of its window (a long-lived flow is no longer re-emitted with its cumulative totals) — console Logs views read the same store. Nano has no data plane at all (no VMs produce real packets), so there is nothing to export there; VLAN attachments and Cloud VPN tunnels aren't modeled.

Public advertised prefixes and public delegated prefixes (regional, with sub-prefix delegation) are real control-plane resources: public-range, size, overlap, containment and announce/withdraw ordering rules are enforced, and deletion is blocked while a prefix is announced or delegated.

features.t: VPC connectivity (Cloud Interconnect, Cloud VPN, Network Connectivity Center)
x: Dedicated/Partner Interconnects and VLAN attachments are real control-plane resources: link type and count limits, location catalog, Cloud Router cross-check against the VPC core, VLAN-tag uniqueness per interconnect, bandwidth against circuit capacity, link-local /29 allocation, partner pairing keys, and delete-in-use rules. Attachment state follows admin state (ACTIVE only when both the attachment and its interconnect are enabled).

Host/service project attachment is real and enforced: projects.enableXpnHost/disableXpnHost/enableXpnResource/disableXpnResource track state with the real constraints (a host can't be disabled while service projects are attached, a project can't serve two hosts, a host can't itself be a service project), and aggregated/usableSubnetworks genuinely returns the host's subnets to an attached service project. Vyomi's Compute core has no real cross-project IAM delegation, and a VM created in a service project cannot actually be placed on the host's shared subnet (gcp_compute_instances_core is single-project).

Connector resources are real: create/list/get/delete, with the real /28 and throughput-range validation and a check that the range doesn't collide with existing subnets/reservations on the network. Vyomi does not run a serverless data plane (Cloud Run/Functions), so no simulated traffic is ever actually routed through a connector.

Policy resources are real: create/list/get/delete, with real validation (mirrored subnetworks must exist on the policy's network, a collector forwarding rule name is required). Offline with netsim enforcement on, real per-packet traffic that matches an enabled policy's mirrored resources + filter is rendered as structured records (core/gcp_compute_core.py:mirrored_packet_log_entries) and written to Cloud Logging — not replicated onto a live collector NIC, since Vyomi has no second network interface to receive a GRE-encapsulated copy.

Routers and their NAT configs are real resources (insert/get/list/patch/delete); a NAT covering a subnet gives its external-IP-less VMs internet egress in Connectivity Tests and, offline with enforcement on, real masquerade. BGP sessions, NAT IP allocation/ports and logging are not modeled.

features.t: Network Intelligence Center — Connectivity Tests (networkmanagement v1)
x: Create / get / list / patch / delete / rerun; reachabilityDetails come from the shared netsim evaluator with START/firewall/route/NAT/DELIVER/DROP steps and drop causes. Round-trip, load balancer, GKE, Cloud SQL and hybrid endpoints are not traced.
